measured.title: Guardrail scanning · 8 rules · single pass vs per-rule regexp
measured.environment: AMD Ryzen 5 5500U (12 threads), Windows, Go 1.26, wazero 1.9 — laptop-class, not the pinned benchmark rig
measured.reading: The Rust-WASM accelerator pays off for large payloads and many rules; at small sizes the WASM call overhead roughly cancels the engine advantage. The bigger real-world win was precompiling rule regexes once instead of per request.

methodology.title: Environment
items: Dedicated vCPU instance, CPU governor performance, nothing else running
Load generator and gateway on the same host; mock backend on loopback
OS, kernel, Go, Rust and Python versions recorded in the run manifest
Each gateway built from a pinned tag; commit SHA recorded
Fresh process per repetition; idle period between runs

methodology.title: Workload
items: Mock OpenAI-shaped backend, fixed think time, fixed-size JSON body
60s per run, warm-up discarded, 5 repetitions, median reported with min/max
Closed-loop concurrency for the table; open-loop stepping for the ceiling
Identical request bodies and headers for every gateway

methodology.title: Fairness controls
items: Default quickstart configs, auth on everywhere, payload logging off everywhere
No OmniSwitch tuning; no competitor detuning; per-gateway config diffs published
Vendor-published numbers are never mixed into our tables
Maintainers of compared projects notified before the run
Managed services excluded — a network hop is not comparable to a local binary

reproduce.note: Run the micro-benchmark that exists today yourself

caveats: Microbenchmarks against a mock. Real providers add hundreds to thousands of ms; a millisecond between gateways will not be visible to users. Tail behaviour under failure will.
One machine, one cloud, once published. Ratios travel better than absolutes — re-run on your own hardware.
Co-located load generator removes network noise but competes for CPU at the ceiling; ceilings will be conservative for everyone.
Default configs differ across gateways. We will publish per-gateway config diffs rather than normalizing features away.
not_claimed: That OmniSwitch is "the fastest gateway". If top results are within noise, we will say so.
Anything about managed services, model quality, cost savings, or cache hit rates on your traffic.
Kubernetes-native strengths of control-plane gateways run standalone.
Stability across versions — every release re-runs the harness once it exists and posts regressions here.
